title: Tashbar Math Ladder, K–8
status: PLAN ONLY, waiting for Mrs. Khaver. Nothing is built from it until she approves it.
asked: Mrs. Khaver (2026-11-23): "Make this K through 8th math ladder plan, and it's a plan only. I want to see it before you start implementing anything. The other ones already have 1 or 2 levels, so we're gonna make the whole ladder, and then we're gonna fill it in based on what we have already, just higher and lower madregos."
how: Math is 10 ladders (strands), side by side. Each ladder has rungs (madregos). Each rung is one real skill, in the order a child's thinking actually grows.
Each rung has a usual grade, but a boy climbs at his own pace. He can be on a Grade 3 rung in adding and a Grade 2 rung in fractions.
A short placement check finds his rung on each ladder. He starts there, not at the start of his grade.
Going up: he passes a rung's check with no help, 2 days apart. Then the next rung opens.
Going down: if he gets stuck twice, he drops one rung for a short re-teach on the skill underneath, then climbs back. This is built into every rung.
Every rung is one unit made to the school's standard: a short, warm opening lesson, then hands-on practice games, a "How to do it" box on every question, and a check.
Old rungs come back in mixed review, so nothing is forgotten.
sources: Building Blocks (Clements & Sarama): learning trajectories, the named levels of thinking for K–2 and early Grade 3. The small grey names under each rung are their level names.
Clements & Sarama, Learning and Teaching Early Math: the research behind those levels.
Common Core Progressions (the writers of the standards): the order of skills from Grade 3 to 8, where Building Blocks stops.
Concrete, then picture, then numbers: every new idea starts with things he can move, then drawings, then numbers.
Bar models (Singapore math) for story problems, Grades 2–7.
Short daily number talks and spaced, mixed review.

key.v1: Lessons in 1.0 we can take, check and remake
key.new: Nothing yet: we build it new

strands.name: Counting and the number line
strands.about: Saying numbers, counting things, counting on and back, skip counting, then the whole number line: negatives, fractions and roots.

rungs.name: Say the numbers to 10
rungs.can: Says 1 to 10 in order, without skipping.
rungs.check: Count with me from 1. Where did you stop?

rungs.name: One number for each thing
rungs.can: Touches each thing once and says one number for it.
rungs.check: Count these 6 apples. Touch each one.

rungs.name: The last number tells how many
rungs.can: After counting, knows the last number is how many there are.
rungs.check: You counted 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. So how many are there?

rungs.name: Give me 7
rungs.can: Counts out a number of things when asked, up to 10, then 20.
rungs.check: Put 7 kugels on the plate.

rungs.name: One more, one less, count back
rungs.bb: Counter Backward from 10; Counter from N (N+1, N–1)
rungs.can: Counts back from 10. Knows the number just after and just before.
rungs.check: There are 6. One more comes. How many now, without counting all?

rungs.name: Count to 100 by ones and tens
rungs.bb: Skip Counter by 10s to 100; Counter to 100
rungs.can: Counts to 100 by ones and by tens.
rungs.check: Count by tens to 100.

rungs.name: Start anywhere and count on
rungs.can: Starts at any number (like 47) and counts on, to 120.
rungs.check: Start at 58. Count on 5.

rungs.name: Skip count by 2s, 5s, 10s, 100s; odd and even
rungs.can: Skip counts from any number. Tells odd from even by pairing.
rungs.check: Count by 5s from 35. Is 14 odd or even? Show me with pairs.

rungs.name: Below zero: negative numbers
rungs.can: Places negatives on the number line and compares them. Uses all four parts of the grid.
rungs.check: Which is colder, –8° or –3°? Put both on the line.

rungs.name: All the numbers on one line (rationals)
rungs.can: Puts fractions, decimals and negatives on one line. Knows which decimals end and which repeat.
rungs.check: Put –1½, 0.75 and –0.3 on the line. Does ⅓ as a decimal end?

rungs.name: Roots and real numbers
rungs.can: Finds square roots, squeezes a root between two whole numbers, knows numbers that never repeat.
rungs.check: √50 is between which two whole numbers?

strands.name: Seeing, comparing and breaking numbers
strands.about: Seeing how many at a glance, comparing amounts, and knowing the parts inside a number. This is the ground that adding stands on.

rungs.name: See 1, 2, 3 at a glance
rungs.can: Says how many (up to 3, then 4) without counting.
rungs.check: Flash 3 dots for one second. How many?

rungs.name: See 5 at a glance
rungs.can: Sees up to 5 at once, in dice or finger patterns.
rungs.check: Flash a 5 on a dice. How many?

rungs.name: More, fewer, the same
rungs.can: Compares two groups by matching or counting, even when one group is spread out.
rungs.check: 7 spread-out cups and 8 close-together cups. Which has more?

rungs.name: Parts of numbers to 5
rungs.can: Knows 5 is 4 and 1, 3 and 2, and so on.
rungs.check: 5 apples, 2 in the bag. How many are hiding?

rungs.name: Parts of 6 to 10; friends of 10
rungs.can: Knows all the pairs that make 10, and the parts of 6 to 9.
rungs.check: 7 on the ten-frame. How many more make 10?

rungs.name: See numbers to 20 in parts
rungs.can: Sees "10 and 4" or "5 and 3" on ten-frames without counting.
rungs.check: Flash two ten-frames (10 and 6). How many?

rungs.name: Compare with < > =
rungs.can: Compares two-digit numbers by tens first, and writes < > =.
rungs.check: Which is more, 49 or 52? Write it with the sign.

strands.name: Adding and subtracting
strands.about: From joining things with his hands, to smart strategies, to big numbers, to negatives.

rungs.name: Put together, take away (within 5)
rungs.can: Solves joining and taking-away stories with things he can move.
rungs.check: Moshe has 3 cookies. Bubby gives him 2. How many now?

rungs.name: Add and take away within 10
rungs.can: Solves stories within 10, including "how many more?".
rungs.check: Yaakov has 4 seforim. He needs 9. How many more?

rungs.name: Count on, count back
rungs.can: Adds by counting on from the bigger number, not from 1.
rungs.check: 8 + 3: start at 8 and hop.

rungs.name: Smart facts: doubles and make ten
rungs.can: Uses doubles, near doubles and make-ten to add and subtract within 20.
rungs.check: 8 + 6: make a ten first. Show me how.

rungs.name: The missing number and the = sign
rungs.can: Knows = means "the same as". Finds a missing number anywhere.

rungs.name: Every kind of story within 20
rungs.can: Solves joining, taking, comparing and missing-part stories, with a drawing.
rungs.check: Chaim has 13 marbles, 5 more than Dovid. How many does Dovid have?

rungs.name: Facts within 20, fast
rungs.can: Knows all facts within 20 quickly, without counting.
rungs.check: 20 mixed facts in 2 minutes.

rungs.name: Add and subtract within 100
rungs.can: Adds and subtracts two-digit numbers with tens and ones, on a number line or in his head.

rungs.name: Within 1,000; two-step stories
rungs.can: Regroups with hundreds. Solves two-step stories with a bar model.
rungs.check: 352 + 179. A story with two steps.

rungs.name: The column method for big numbers
rungs.can: Adds and subtracts numbers to a million in columns, and checks with an estimate.
rungs.check: 40,006 – 18,297. Is your answer sensible?

rungs.name: Adding and subtracting decimals
rungs.can: Adds and subtracts decimals to hundredths by lining up the places.

rungs.name: Adding and subtracting negatives
rungs.can: Adds and subtracts with negative numbers on a number line.

strands.name: Place value and big numbers
strands.about: Tens and ones, then hundreds, thousands and millions, then tenths and hundredths. Each place is 10 times the next.

rungs.name: Teen numbers: ten and some more
rungs.can: Sees 14 as one ten and 4 ones.
rungs.check: Show 16 with a ten-stick and cubes.

rungs.name: Tens and ones to 100
rungs.bb: Counter of Quantitative Units / Place Value
rungs.can: Builds and reads any two-digit number as tens and ones.
rungs.check: How many tens in 73? Build it.

rungs.name: 10 more, 10 less
rungs.can: Finds 10 more or 10 less in his head.
rungs.check: 10 less than 64?

rungs.name: Hundreds, tens and ones
rungs.can: Reads, writes, builds and compares numbers to 1,000, in expanded form too.
rungs.check: Write 406 as hundreds + tens + ones. Compare 406 and 460.

rungs.name: Round to 10 and 100
rungs.can: Rounds on a number line and uses it to estimate.
rungs.check: Round 348 to the nearest ten and the nearest hundred.

rungs.name: Big numbers to a million
rungs.can: Knows each place is 10 times the next. Reads, compares and rounds big numbers.
rungs.check: How many times bigger is the 7 in 7,000 than the 7 in 700?

rungs.name: Decimals and powers of ten
rungs.can: Reads, compares and rounds decimals to thousandths. Multiplies and divides by 10, 100, 1,000.
rungs.check: Which is more, 0.4 or 0.38? 3.6 × 100?

rungs.name: Exponents and scientific notation
rungs.can: Uses powers and writes very big and very small numbers in scientific notation.
rungs.check: Write 45,000,000 in scientific notation.

strands.name: Multiplying and dividing
strands.about: From fair sharing with things, to equal groups and arrays, to facts, to long multiplication and division.

rungs.name: Fair sharing
rungs.can: Shares things fairly, one for you, one for me, and checks it is fair.
rungs.check: Share 8 pretzels fairly between 2 brothers.

rungs.name: Equal groups and arrays
rungs.bb: Grouper and Distributive Sharer; Skip Counter ×/÷
rungs.can: Counts equal groups by skip counting. Sees rows and columns.
rungs.check: 4 rows of 5 chairs. How many chairs?

rungs.name: What × means
rungs.can: Knows 3 × 4 means 3 groups of 4, and the order does not change the answer.
rungs.check: Draw 3 × 4 two ways.

rungs.name: What ÷ means
rungs.can: Knows dividing as sharing and as making groups. Uses a times fact to divide.
rungs.check: 24 hamantaschen, 6 on each plate. How many plates?

rungs.name: Times facts with strategies
rungs.can: Uses easy facts to find hard ones (double the 2s to get the 4s). Knows all facts to 10 × 10.
rungs.check: You know 5 × 7. How does it help with 6 × 7?

rungs.name: Times tens; four-step stories
rungs.can: Multiplies by 10s (4 × 60). Solves stories with any of the four operations.
rungs.check: 8 × 40. A story that needs × then –.

rungs.name: Multi-digit × and ÷ with leftovers
rungs.can: Multiplies up to 4 digits by 1 digit and 2 by 2 with an area model. Divides with remainders and decides what the leftover means.
rungs.check: 23 × 14. 50 boys, 6 to a van: how many vans?

rungs.name: Factors, multiples, primes
rungs.can: Finds all factor pairs of a number to 100. Tells prime from composite.
rungs.check: All the factors of 36. Is 29 prime?

rungs.name: Big multiplying, two-digit dividing, decimals
rungs.can: Multiplies fluently. Divides by 2-digit numbers. Multiplies and divides decimals to hundredths.

rungs.name: Long division, decimals, GCF and LCM
rungs.can: Divides fluently, all decimal operations, greatest common factor and least common multiple.

rungs.name: Multiplying and dividing negatives
rungs.can: Multiplies and divides positive and negative numbers and fractions.

strands.name: Fractions, decimals, ratio and percent
strands.about: From fair halves of a challah, to fractions on the number line, to all four operations, to ratio and percent.

rungs.name: Halves and quarters
rungs.can: Cuts a shape into 2 or 4 equal parts and names them.
rungs.check: Cut the challah into 4 fair pieces. What is one piece called?

rungs.name: Halves, thirds, fourths
rungs.can: Makes equal shares and knows equal shares can look different.
rungs.check: Two ways to cut a square into halves.

rungs.name: Fractions are numbers
rungs.can: Knows ¼ is 1 of 4 equal parts. Puts fractions on the number line, including whole numbers as fractions.
rungs.check: Put ¾ on the number line. 4/4 = ?

rungs.name: Compare and find equal fractions
rungs.can: Compares fractions with the same top or bottom. Finds equal fractions with a model.
rungs.check: Which is more, ⅓ or ⅕? Why?

rungs.name: Add and subtract like fractions; mixed numbers
rungs.can: Adds and subtracts fractions with the same bottom number, and mixed numbers.

rungs.name: Tenths and hundredths
rungs.can: Writes tenths and hundredths as decimals and compares them.

rungs.name: Unlike fractions
rungs.can: Adds and subtracts fractions with different bottom numbers.
rungs.check: ⅔ + ¼.

rungs.name: Multiply and divide fractions
rungs.can: Multiplies a fraction by a whole number and by a fraction. Divides with unit fractions, then any fraction.
rungs.check: ¾ of 12. ½ ÷ 4. ⅔ ÷ ⅜.

rungs.name: Ratios, rates and percent
rungs.can: Uses ratio tables and unit rates. Finds a percent of a number.
rungs.check: 3 bottles cost $6. What do 7 cost? 20% of 45?

rungs.name: Proportions and percent problems
rungs.can: Spots proportional relationships. Solves discount, tax and tip problems.
rungs.check: A $40 coat is 15% off. What does it cost?

strands.name: Patterns and algebra
strands.about: From AB patterns on a bead string, to number rules, to expressions, equations and graphs.

rungs.name: Copy and continue AB patterns
rungs.bb: Pattern Duplicator AB; Pattern Extender AB
rungs.can: Copies and continues red-blue-red-blue.
rungs.check: What comes next? Finish the bead string.

rungs.name: The part that repeats
rungs.can: Finds the core of ABB and ABC patterns, fixes a broken one, makes his own.
rungs.check: Circle the part that repeats.

rungs.name: Number patterns
rungs.can: Continues and explains patterns like 5, 10, 15 or +10 on a hundred chart.
rungs.check: 14, 24, 34, __. What is the rule?

rungs.name: Patterns with a rule
rungs.can: Finds and explains the rule in a number pattern and a times table.
rungs.check: Why is every multiple of 5 ending in 0 or 5?

rungs.name: Write expressions; two patterns on a graph
rungs.can: Writes expressions with brackets. Makes two patterns and graphs them.
rungs.check: Write: add 8 and 7, then times 2.

rungs.name: Letters for numbers; one-step equations
rungs.can: Writes and works out expressions with a letter. Solves one-step equations.
rungs.check: x + 9 = 23. What is 3n when n = 4?

rungs.name: Two-step equations
rungs.can: Solves two-step equations and simplifies expressions, with negatives and fractions.

rungs.name: Functions, slope and straight lines
rungs.can: Knows what a function is. Finds slope. Graphs and writes y = mx + b.
rungs.check: Graph y = 2x + 1. What is the slope?

rungs.name: Two equations at once
rungs.can: Solves a system of two linear equations by graph and by reasoning.
rungs.check: x + y = 10 and x – y = 2.

strands.name: Shapes and space
strands.about: From naming shapes by their rules, to building with shapes, to angles, area, volume and the Pythagorean theorem.

rungs.name: Name shapes by their rules
rungs.can: Names circle, triangle, square and rectangle in any size or turn.
rungs.check: Find all the triangles, even the upside-down one.

rungs.name: Sides and corners; tricky look-alikes
rungs.can: Counts sides and corners. Knows a shape with a gap or a curve is not a triangle.
rungs.check: Is this a triangle? Why not?

rungs.name: Solid shapes
rungs.can: Names sphere, cube, cylinder and cone, and knows flat from solid.
rungs.check: Which one rolls? Which stacks?

rungs.name: Where is it?
rungs.can: Uses on top, under, next to, in front of, behind.
rungs.check: Put the cup behind the box.

rungs.name: Build shapes from shapes
rungs.can: Puts shapes together to make new shapes and pictures, and plans which piece goes where.
rungs.check: Make a hexagon with triangles.

rungs.name: Rows and columns; cutting rectangles
rungs.can: Cuts a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares and counts them.
rungs.check: Fill this rectangle with squares. How many?

rungs.name: Four-sided shape families
rungs.can: Sorts quadrilaterals by their properties. Knows a square is also a rectangle.
rungs.check: Is a square a rectangle? Prove it.

rungs.name: Angles, lines and symmetry
rungs.can: Measures and draws angles with a protractor. Finds parallel lines and lines of symmetry.
rungs.check: Measure this angle. Draw a line of symmetry.

rungs.name: The coordinate grid; shape hierarchy
rungs.can: Plots points on a grid. Places shapes in a family tree by their properties.
rungs.check: Plot (3, 5). Every rhombus is a ___?

rungs.name: Area of triangles; nets
rungs.can: Finds the area of triangles and other shapes by cutting them up. Uses nets for surface area.
rungs.check: Area of a triangle with base 8 and height 5.

rungs.name: Scale drawings, circles, angle facts
rungs.can: Uses scale drawings. Circle area and circumference. Solves angle, area and volume problems.
rungs.check: Area of a circle with radius 3.

rungs.name: Slide, turn, flip; Pythagoras; round solids
rungs.can: Moves shapes by slides, turns and flips. Uses a² + b² = c². Volume of cylinders, cones and spheres.
rungs.check: A ladder 13 ft long, foot 5 ft from the wall. How high does it reach?

strands.name: Measuring, time and money
strands.about: From lining things up to compare, to units with no gaps, to rulers, area, volume and converting units.

rungs.name: Longer, shorter, taller
rungs.can: Compares lengths by lining things up from the same start.
rungs.check: Which pencil is longer? Line them up first.

rungs.name: Heavier, lighter, holds more
rungs.can: Compares weight on a balance and how much cups hold.
rungs.check: Which is heavier? Look at the balance.

rungs.name: Measure with units, no gaps
rungs.bb: End-to-End Length Measurer; Length Unit Iterater
rungs.can: Measures with same-size units laid end to end, with no gaps or overlaps.
rungs.check: How many paper clips long is the pencil?

rungs.name: Clock to the half hour; coins
rungs.can: Tells time to the half hour. Names coins and their values.
rungs.check: What time is it? How much is a dime?

rungs.name: Rulers: inches and centimeters
rungs.can: Measures with a ruler starting at 0. Finds how much longer.
rungs.check: Measure the line. How much longer is the blue one?

rungs.name: Time to 5 minutes; money and change
rungs.can: Tells time to 5 minutes. Counts money and makes change.
rungs.check: You pay $1 for a 65¢ snack. What change?

rungs.name: Area and perimeter
rungs.can: Finds area by squares and then by multiplying. Finds perimeter.
rungs.check: Area and perimeter of a 6 × 4 room.

rungs.name: Time passed; liters and grams
rungs.can: Finds how long something took. Measures liquid and weight in metric units.
rungs.check: Davening starts 8:15, ends 8:50. How long?

rungs.name: Convert units; area and perimeter formulas
rungs.can: Changes feet to inches, hours to minutes. Uses area and perimeter formulas.
rungs.check: 3 ft 4 in = ? in.

rungs.name: Volume; metric conversions
rungs.bb: Volume Unit Relater (Building Blocks) to Progressions
rungs.can: Finds volume by packing cubes, then by length × width × height. Converts metric units.
rungs.check: Volume of a 4 × 3 × 2 box.

rungs.name: Convert with ratios
rungs.can: Uses ratio reasoning to convert any units.
rungs.check: 60 miles in 1 hour. How far in 20 minutes?

strands.name: Data and chance
strands.about: From sorting toys into bins, to graphs, to average and spread, to probability.

rungs.name: Sort and count
rungs.can: Sorts by color, size or shape, counts each group, and says which has more.
rungs.check: Sort the toys. Which bin has the most?

rungs.name: Picture graphs
rungs.can: Reads and makes a picture graph and answers "how many more?".
rungs.check: How many more boys picked apples than pears?

rungs.name: Bar graphs
rungs.can: Makes and reads bar graphs and answers two-step questions.
rungs.check: Make a bar graph of 4 groups.

rungs.name: Graphs with a scale
rungs.can: Reads graphs where one picture stands for 2, 5 or 10.
rungs.check: Each star stands for 5. How many?

rungs.name: Line plots with fractions
rungs.can: Makes line plots of measurements in halves, quarters and eighths.
rungs.check: Plot these lengths: 2¼, 2½, 2¼, 3.

rungs.name: Average and spread
rungs.can: Finds mean, median and range. Reads dot plots, histograms and box plots.
rungs.check: Scores 6, 8, 8, 9, 14: mean and median?

rungs.name: Samples and chance
rungs.can: Uses a fair sample to guess about a group. Finds the probability of simple events.
rungs.check: A bag has 3 red and 5 blue. Chance of red?

rungs.name: Scatter plots and two-way tables
rungs.can: Draws a trend line on a scatter plot. Reads two-way tables.
rungs.check: Does more practice mean higher scores? Draw the line.

next: Mrs. Khaver reads the ladder and says what to add, remove, move or rename.
When she approves the plan, we fill it rung by rung, one small piece at a time, each with its own look link and her yes.
For each rung we first look at what already exists (2.0 or 1.0), keep what is good, fix what is not, and build what is missing.
The Kindergarten Numbers and Shapes plans already fill most K rungs. Next come the rungs just above them (Grade 1) and the rungs below where a boy needs help.
